WARM-UP

Basketball School

I-ON-1 ELBOW RACE

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets (ideally a maximum of eight players per basket)

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per player.

### DESCRIPTION

Players will begin at the elbows. They must begin at the same time, completing two crossover dribbles, before racing to the basket to score a lay-up. Players must keep shooting until one player scores. Once both players finish, they should move off around the side while new players begin immediately.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Use a smaller ball.
- Three through-the-legs then finish only with their left hand.
- Three waist wraps then finish only using the net.
- Five dribble pounds then finish only using the backboard under-handed.

### SCORING

The first player to score gains 1 point.

### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players rotate quickly to save time and increase time-on-task.
- Remind players to successfully complete the load.
- Change angles at any time (e.g. instead of coming from the elbows, attack from the short corner and elbow).

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creative finishing
- Developing ball manipulation skills

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

"How can you organize yourselves to ensure you start at the same time?"

MODULE 4: FULL OUTLINE

WARM-UP

Basketball School

I-ON-I SLALOM

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

2 balls and 3 cones per group of 4 players

### DESCRIPTION

One cone will be laid out in front of the 3PT line, in any location. The second cone will be laid inside the 3PT line, one big step from the first cone. The third cone will be placed one big step beyond this second cone. Two players will wait standing over the second and third cones, facing the rim. An offensive player will begin facing the cones, four big steps behind the first cone. One additional player with a ball will stand an arm distance behind the offensive player. As soon as the lead offensive player starts, both players must dribble slalom through the cones and the waiting players. The goal is to score inside the smile first.

### SCORING

The first player to score a lay-up inside the smile gains 1 point.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creative finishing
- Developing ball manipulation skills
- Developing functional movements

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Players can only score with their weak hand.
- Lead player can pick a movement to go through the slalom which the second player must shadow (e.g. hops, skips, moving sideways, etc).
- Players have six dribbles to get through the slalom and into the smile.
- The second player does not hold a ball and waits an arm distance behind the offensive player. They become a live defender and must slalom through the obstacle course before stopping the offense.
- The offensive player does not hold a ball, which instead is held by the player standing over the cone closest to the basket. As the offense approaches the player with the ball, they may receive the ball through a hand-off to score.

### STAFF ROLE

- Help players set-up their slalom courses.
- Ensure players understand the activity while rotating quickly.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- Can you explore using different movements to creatively navigate the obstacles?

GAME TIME

Basketball School

## GAME TIME

is where players participate in different activities and games designed to stimulate their growth and development.

These activities have been carefully created to mimic the game of basketball. With the NBA Basketball School Camp Curriculum, players develop technically and tactically through the actual act of playing basketball itself.

Each Game Time activity is clearly described and presented in the following format: name, time, space, equipment, description, scoring, types of loads, staff roles, key concepts, and guiding questions. Coaches are encouraged to utilize the information presented and to expand on those ideas in a way that would be most meaningful to their players.

### VARIABLE SHOOTING

2-ON-2 LINE START TO POST-UPS

1-ON-1 GUIDED POST-UPS

3-ON-2 SHOOTING

5-ON-5 LOADS-BASED

GAME TIME

Basketball School

VARIABLE SHOOTING

IG MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group.

#### DESCRIPTION

Players work in pairs. The shooter shoots six shots and their partner rebounds. Once six shots are taken, players change roles. To begin with, players focus on shooting every shot from a different range and location, while passing in a variable manner in different ways and from changing locations and distances.

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Use a smaller ball and shoot from a closer distance.
- Players must shoot with different arcs (low arc, normal arc, high arc).
- Players must shoot from different stances (wide, narrow, one leg, staggered, etc).
- Players must shoot while performing a different dribble move before each shot.
- Players must shoot out of different movements (e.g. lunges, hops, crawls, hand-stands, etc).

#### SCORING

N/A

#### STAFF ROLE

- Encourage players to explore different shooting coordinations.
- Remind players to continuously change where they shoot and pass from.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Adaptive shooting

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- How can you make each movement more variable?

GAME TIME

Basketball School

### 2-ON-2 LINE START TO POST-UPS

IG MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Begin with an offensive player holding a ball and under the basket, facing the 3PT line. A defender will stand behind them, followed by another offensive player and another more defender behind (alternating offense and defense). The first offensive player will dribble to any five-out spacing location to begin the activity. The second offensive player will look to post-up on the strongside block. Once the ball-handler reaches the perimeter, they may make a post entry pass into their teammate, or drive, based on where they think the advantage exists. A live 2-on-2 is then played. If there is a change of possession (defensive rebound or forced turnover), the roles switch. Keep playing until a team scores.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Disruptive defense
- Post-up positioning and passing
- Square stance in the post to reduce turnovers on post entry pass (vs. 45 degree angle)

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- One defender on each team must play defense with their hands behind their back, but they are allowed to rebound.
- Turnover called if the post catches the ball too far from the basket. This occurs if the ball is caught higher than the block or one step outside of the block (e.g. the short corner).
- Offense receives double points if they score off a cut to the post.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Demonstrate how players can dig at post.
- Remind players to work to establish deep post-up positioning: close to the smile (within the three second count) or on the strongside block.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- How can you disrupt the pass into the post?
- How can you defend the post to prevent a straight line score?

GAME TIME

Basketball School

I-ON-I GUIDED POST-UPS

IG MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Players will work in pairs. The offensive player will begin near the smile, self-spinning the ball out to the strongside block. They will catch the ball square to the baseline. As they catch the ball, the defender must influence the post clearly, either sending the post player middle or baseline. The defender will then wall-up and contest the shot, as the post player takes one dribble towards the rim to score. Complete two repetitions then switch roles. Two groups can play at each basket. If there are high numbers, have a third group spin the ball towards free-throw line and play with the same options from the mid-post.

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, allow more dribbles.
- The guided defense will only provide the read when the offensive player faces-up by pivoting to face the basket.
- Add a third read of neutral. This means the defense could influence middle, influence baseline, or show neutral.
- Give the offense a one dribble limit.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players catch the ball square.
- Help defenders make sure the reads they give are clear for the offense to read.
- Ensure players do not travel (especially when moving towards the face-up part of the activity).

#### SCORING

N/A

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Making quick decisions against the guided defense
- Catching square to the baseline
- Practicing legal post defense with one arm-bar and one hand in air
- Defense showing hands on face-up
- Walling-up and contesting on shots from post

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- Can you try to catch the ball in the post while taking a look at your defender?
- How can you protect the ball from your defender?
